dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the ISA, simulator, and reference kernel

evidence.note: Before any edit, read problem.py (simulator/ISA), the reference kernel.py, run_tests.sh, and submission_tests.py — a complete upfront decode of the environment, correctness contract, and cost harness.
Inspected memory layout and level sequence and enumerated repo files, extending the model of the data/computation the reference must reproduce beyond a surface skim.

Empirically measured per-engine slot usage, engine floors, and bundle occupancy across MUX_MAX/ALU_VECTORS — building an accurate quantitative model of SLOT_LIMITS and the per-slot cost model rather than assuming it.

Mid-optimization returned to source to print hash stages, derive hash-stage algebra, and find env usages — treating problem.py as ground truth to resolve data-dependency ambiguities as they arose, characteristic of the top anchor.

dimensions.reasoning: The action arc shows a thorough upfront read of problem.py, the reference kernel, and the test harness, followed by empirical decoding of per-engine slot limits, op costs, and bundle occupancy, and later re-derivation of the hash-stage algebra directly from source (198, 212) mid-optimization — matching the level-8 'precise model of slot limits, op costs, and hash-stage dependencies' plus the level-10 habit of revisiting the source to resolve ambiguities. I withhold a 9-10 because the trajectory exposes only action headers, so I cannot confirm the depth of the restated numeric contract, and the explicit lower-bound/split reasoning belongs to a different facet.

dimensions.name: Staging the 118x speedup into checkpoints

evidence.note: Understanding phase (reads problem/kernel/tests, runs baseline, inspects memory layout) precedes optimization, giving a known-good starting point.
TaskCreate lays out an upfront decomposition of transformations (vectorize lanes, optimize hash via multiply_add, scalar gather) — phase identification, but no intermediate cycle gates.
One large rewrite folds correct+vectorize+packing together, measured at step 31; the agent jumped past intermediate rungs (<20k, <5k) rather than climbing an explicit ladder.
Late campaign chases specific quantitative targets (slack profiles at 1250, 1225, 1211) with continual measurement, showing gate-chasing near the end.
Recurring edits to vliw-kernel-task.md indicate sustained progress tracking across the whole arc, though not a rung-by-rung preserved milestone ladder.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent identified a few phases upfront (TaskCreate plan) and worked them roughly in order — understand, one big correct+vectorized rewrite, then a long packing/scheduling optimization toward the target — with a known-good baseline and ongoing progress notes, matching the level-5 anchor. It did not maintain an explicit quantitative milestone ladder (<20k, <5k, <1250) with a preserved known-good version at each rung; the correct/vectorized/packed transforms were collapsed into a single leap rather than sequenced gates, so it stays below level 8. Only late in the run did it chase discrete numeric checkpoints (1250→1225→1211).

'Measure per-engine slot usage' and 'Bundle occupancy histograms' — independent inspection of slot-limit legality / bundle occupancy beyond run_tests.sh.
Repeated dedicated correctness checks after transformations (mux fold, DIAGW, prefetch), verifying each change didn't break results before proceeding.
'Repeat correctness for robustness' — deliberately re-runs correctness across randomized inputs rather than trusting one green run.
'Verify instrs format' — independent check that self.instrs meets the plain-list legality rule, a targeted check the provided test doesn't foreground.
Layered final verification: full suite, kernel built-in tests, verify from /app, final official run.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently pairs correctness and cycle verification after meaningful changes (steps 31, 204-206, 217, 236, 253) and re-runs correctness for randomized robustness (284), clearing anchor 5. It also builds tighter-than-provided feedback — per-engine slot usage, occupancy histograms, and an independent instrs-format legality check (34, 68, 321) — matching anchor 8's 'verify slot-limit legality independently before the full test.' It stops short of anchor 10 because the correctness ground truth remains the provided test re-run, with no self-built differential harness isolating individual hash stages against the reference.

dimensions.name: Tracking cycles-to-target and detecting plateaus

evidence.note: Cycle count tracked across iterations with explicit falling numbers tied to target: baseline test, 'Utilization at 1250', 'Floors and slack at 1225', 'Slack profile at 1211' — accurate running picture of distance to 1250.

Computes critical-path lower bound, 'minimum analysis', and optimal valu/alu split — quantitative floor reasoning used to gauge remaining headroom and reprioritize (plateau/diminishing-returns awareness).
Repeated idle/utilization/region-breakdown profiling at each new cycle level shows continuous reprioritization toward the largest remaining bottleneck.
Recurring updates to vliw-kernel-task.md memory file indicate a sustained written ledger of results/state across the long horizon.

Pivots across distinct attack lines (scheduler modes, priority boost, arithmetic mux, diagonal, prefetch) each followed by measurement; a couple of re-sweeps (MUX_MAX, DIAGW) hint at minor circular re-tuning short of the level-10 anchor.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintained an accurate, numeric picture of current cycles vs the 1250 target (explicitly citing 1250→1225→1211), repeatedly computed theoretical floors/slack, and profiled engine utilization to steer effort toward the binding bottleneck, pivoting between optimization lines after measuring each — matching the level-8 anchor (attributing deltas, noticing stalled lines, pivoting). It approaches level-10 with a persistent ledger and floor-vs-actual reasoning, but the evidence (descriptions only, no prose) does not confirm explicit diminishing-returns recognition, and a few re-sweeps suggest some circular re-tuning, so it falls just below 10 at 8.

dimensions.name: Revising approach when a transformation fails or backfires

evidence.note: Early strategy pivots each gated by measurement: ALU_VECTORS offload sweep + per-engine totals, then a switch to an 'offset representation' re-evaluated via 'engine floors with offset rep' — adjusting the approach based on measured engine floors, not blind edits.

Successive distinct scheduling strategies (auto-balancer -> critical-path scheduler -> priority modes), each followed by floor/occupancy measurement, showing the agent abandoning one tactic for another informed by prior measurements.

Concentrated root-cause diagnosis: classify binding engine per cycle, per-engine idle/utilization analysis, critical-path lower bound, engine full-cycle counts per region. This is diagnosing which resource actually binds and redirecting optimization there — the hallmark of the level-8 anchor.

Continued informed pivots (per-round balancing, emission-order tests, diagonal-width DIAGW sweeps) interleaved with slack-location and region-breakdown analysis, plus repeated correctness checks (204-206, 217, 236) guarding against breaking the kernel while transforming.

Late consolidation: balancer-reset and fifocp-tiebreak toggle tests, then 'bare run no env vars' and final verification, indicating convergence on a fixed known-good config rather than leaving falsified experimental knobs active.

dimensions.reasoning: The action sequence shows a consistent measure-diagnose-redirect loop: the agent repeatedly swaps whole scheduling/packing strategies and each swap is bracketed by targeted diagnostics (binding-engine classification, idle analysis, critical-path lower bound) that identify which resource is limiting — matching the level-8 anchor of diagnosing the root cause and redirecting the plan. It falls short of 9-10 because the available evidence (action titles only, no observation text) does not show explicit revert-to-known-good-baseline after a regression or decisive re-derivation of the milestone ladder, so I place it at 7, above the simple 'revert and try another tactic' level (5) but not fully at the model-updating 8.

dimensions.name: Quantitative bottleneck / lower-bound reasoning

evidence.note: Repeated per-engine slot-usage measurement and 'engine floors' computation establishes slot-port lower bounds early and uses them to pick offload levels (ALU_VECTORS sweeps).

Classifies the binding engine per cycle, computes a critical-path (dependency-latency) lower bound, and does per-region engine full-cycle counts — identifying which resource actually bounds each region.
Work-volume analysis: counts muladd vs simple ops and total logical vector ops, tying work volume to a bundle/cycle floor.

'Floors and slack at 1225', 'Compute minimum analysis', 'Optimal valu/alu split calculation', and 'Slack profile at 1211' show a maintained floor-vs-actual model used to judge remaining headroom as the kernel nears the target.

dimensions.reasoning: Across the entire trajectory the agent repeatedly computes defensible lower bounds from both slot limits (per-engine floors) and dependency latency (critical-path lower bound), classifies the binding engine per cycle/region, quantifies work volume, and tracks slack against the floor at multiple cycle counts — directing edits at the resource the bound identifies. This clearly exceeds anchor 8 and approaches the sustained roofline model of anchor 10 (SIMD width + slot ports + dependency latency + headroom judgment); I hold at 9 only because the log shows command titles rather than the raw numeric reasoning, leaving the sharpness of the model partly unverified.

rubric.task_read: An extremely long-horizon, high-difficulty optimization task: reverse-engineer an undocumented custom VLIW SIMD ISA + simulator (problem.py, SLOT_LIMITS, HASH_STAGES, reference kernel) and rewrite /app/kernel.py to run a ~118x faster (147,734 → <1250 cycles) kernel that stays correct on randomized inputs. Difficulty comes from (a) deep understanding of an unfamiliar machine model and the reference semantics, and (b) sustained, quantitatively-driven optimization — vectorization, bundle/slot packing, scheduling — where naive effort plateaus far short of the target. This warrants heavy, sustained meta-work across all five faculties.

dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the ISA, simulator, and reference kernel
dimensions.description: Reading problem.py to build an accurate model of the machine — ISA/opcodes, per-slot limits, hash stages, cycle-cost model — and inferring exactly what the reference kernel must compute.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The entire optimization space, correctness contract, and cost model are latent in problem.py; every downstream decision (which ops are cheap, how many slots per bundle, what result must match) depends on how accurately the agent decodes the environment before and while optimizing.

anchors.0: Edits kernel.py without reading problem.py or the reference kernel; guesses at the ISA.
anchors.3: Skims problem.py; grasps a few opcodes but misunderstands slot limits, the cost model, or what the kernel must output.
anchors.5: Reads the simulator and reference kernel enough to enumerate available ops, understand the per-cycle/per-slot cost model, and correctly restate the computation to be reproduced.
anchors.8: Builds a precise mental (or written) model: exact SLOT_LIMITS per unit, cost of each op class, data dependencies of the hash stages, and the numeric contract the output must satisfy — and cites specific lines/behaviors to justify it.
anchors.10: Derives a near-complete quantitative machine model (what a bundle can issue per cycle, which resource is scarcest, where the reference wastes cycles) and revisits problem.py to resolve specific ambiguities as they arise mid-optimization, treating the source as ground truth rather than assumption.

dimensions.name: Staging the 118x speedup into checkpoints
dimensions.description: Breaking the huge gap into an ordered ladder — e.g. correct rewrite → vectorized → slot-packed/scheduled → target — each with a concrete cycle/correctness checkpoint, rather than one undifferentiated optimization push.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A ~118x reduction is unreachable in one leap; without intermediate targets and a known-good baseline to fall back to, the agent cannot tell which transformation bought which savings or recover from a regression.

anchors.0: No sub-goals; blindly tweaks the kernel hoping the number drops.
anchors.3: Vague ordering ('make it faster') with no explicit intermediate targets or done-criteria.
anchors.5: Identifies a few phases (get correct first, then vectorize, then pack) and works them roughly in order.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit milestone ladder with quantitative gates (e.g. 'correct baseline', '<20k', '<5k', '<1250') and a preserved known-good version at each rung.
anchors.10: Milestones are derived from the cost model (each targets a specific bottleneck with an estimated cycle payoff), sequenced by dependency and expected ROI, and revised as measurements reveal where the real cycles are.

dimensions.name: Correctness + cycle verification beyond run_tests.sh
dimensions.description: Deliberately designing checks that catch both correctness regressions (across randomized inputs) and cycle changes, rather than trusting a single final test run.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Aggressive SIMD/packing transformations silently break correctness or violate slot limits; a tight, frequent verification loop is what separates real progress from a fast-but-wrong kernel.

anchors.0: Never runs run_tests.sh, or only at the very end; no correctness checking during changes.
anchors.3: Runs the provided test occasionally; treats a green run as sufficient and does no independent correctness reasoning.
anchors.5: Runs run_tests.sh after meaningful changes and checks both correctness and the cycle count before proceeding.
anchors.8: Builds tighter feedback than provided: diffs against the reference on custom/edge inputs, isolates sub-computations, and verifies slot-limit legality of bundles independently before the full test.
anchors.10: Maintains a layered verification harness — fast unit checks on individual stages, randomized differential testing vs. the reference, and per-transformation cycle attribution — so any regression is caught and localized immediately rather than discovered at the end.

dimensions.name: Tracking cycles-to-target and detecting plateaus
dimensions.description: Keeping an accurate running picture of current cycle count vs. the 1250 target and whether recent edits are still yielding gains or thrashing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Over a long optimization horizon it is easy to burn effort on transformations that don't move the number; recognizing a plateau or a regression early is what prevents wasted cycles of engineering.

anchors.0: Loses track of the current cycle count or whether changes helped; no sense of distance to target.
anchors.3: Knows the latest number but not the trend; repeats ineffective tweaks without noticing.
anchors.5: Tracks cycle count across iterations and knows roughly how far from 1250, adjusting effort accordingly.
anchors.8: Attributes cycle deltas to specific changes, notices when a line of attack has stopped paying off, and pivots rather than grinding on it.
anchors.10: Sustains a quantitative ledger of where cycles are spent vs. the theoretical floor, continuously reprioritizing toward the largest remaining bottleneck and explicitly recognizing diminishing returns or circular re-tuning.

dimensions.name: Revising approach when a transformation fails or backfires
dimensions.description: Changing the optimization or scheduling strategy when measurements contradict expectations (a packing breaks slot limits, a rewrite regresses cycles, an assumed op is expensive).
dimensions.why_it_matters: The cost model has surprises; barrelling ahead on a falsified assumption (e.g. a bundle that can't legally issue, or a 'vectorization' that costs more) wastes the long horizon and can strand the kernel in a broken state.

anchors.0: Repeats the same failing approach; ignores contradicting test results.
anchors.3: Reacts to failures with random tweaks rather than diagnosing why the assumption was wrong.
anchors.5: When a change regresses or breaks, reverts and tries a different tactic informed by the failure.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the root cause of a divergence (which slot/cost assumption was wrong), updates the machine model, and redirects the plan accordingly.
anchors.10: Treats surprises as evidence that refines the cost model, abandons whole strategies decisively when the data warrants, and re-derives the milestone ladder from the corrected understanding — without losing the known-good baseline.

dimensions.name: Quantitative bottleneck / lower-bound reasoning
dimensions.description: Reasoning explicitly about the theoretical cycle floor and which hardware resource (slots, ports, dependency chains) bounds performance, to steer optimization toward what actually matters.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A 118x target is only reachable by targeting the binding constraint; roofline-style reasoning about the minimum bundles needed and the scarcest slot distinguishes principled optimization from trial-and-error tweaking.

anchors.0: No reasoning about limits; purely empirical poking.
anchors.3: Hand-wavy 'this should be faster' with no quantitative basis.
anchors.5: Estimates roughly how many bundles the work needs and which op class dominates, using that to pick targets.
anchors.8: Computes a defensible lower bound on cycles from the work volume and slot limits, and directs effort at the resource that bound identifies.
anchors.10: Maintains a sharp roofline-style model (min bundles given SIMD width, slot ports, and dependency latency), uses it to judge how close to optimal the kernel is, and knows when further effort is futile vs. when headroom remains.
